cur.behavior: Seen once, then gone; trackers follow the wrong trail.

cur.name: Snowfield watcher
cur.reading: Curse trades speed for toughness, and Mean Look pins a target with a stare so it can't flee. A lineage that holds still on open snow and stares down whatever approaches, rather than retreating. Fits high snowfields like Platinum's Mt. Coronet slopes.
cur.behavior: Stands motionless on a snow ridge, watching the valley for days.

cur.name: Sky-joy flier
cur.reading: The wheeling, flame-spouting flight the entries describe as joy: a dance and a whirlwind. A lineage that flies for display as much as travel. Fits open skies over mountains.
cur.behavior: Wheels and loops over its range on clear days.

cur.name: Cliff-diver
cur.reading: A lineage of the Bagon that never stopped hurling itself off cliffs: a full-body dragon charge, a rampage and a fiery bite. The most likely to lose all thought when angered. Fits sheer cliffs and ravines.
cur.behavior: Dives from height at whatever angers it.

cur.name: Troop helper
cur.reading: Infernape's cooperative lineage in the young: moves that help a partner and borrow a partner's moves. A Chimchar raised in a pack that works together. Fits crags where a troop shares the few good ledges.
cur.behavior: Sticks close to its troop; joins in rather than leads.

cur.name: Four-limb striker
cur.reading: The line's fighting lineage, showing early: fire carried into the hands and feet before Infernape grows its fiery hands. A Chimchar that fights with its limbs, not its tail. Fits cliff faces where a fight is close and footing matters.
cur.behavior: Punches and kicks with a flare of fire; a fighter from the egg.

cur.name: Cliff trickster
cur.reading: Infernape's tricky lineage at the pack stage: Encore locks a rival into repeating itself, Counter turns its blow back, Focus Energy readies the decisive hit. A Monferno that rises in rank by outwitting rivals rather than outburning them.
cur.behavior: Wins rank fights with timing; small fire, high rank.

cur.name: Wall-runner
cur.reading: A lineage that fights from above and with its feet: kicks and a first-strike flinch, matching the entries' launches from walls and ceilings. Fits caves and overhangs.
cur.behavior: Drops from the ceiling feet first.

cur.name: Four-limb striker
cur.reading: The canon fighting style made heritable: burning fists, a burning kick, and a two-footed kick. A lineage that commits to close striking with hands and feet rather than flame at range. Fits narrow ledges where there's no room to keep distance.
cur.behavior: Closes in fast and strikes with every limb; uses its fire as a glove, not a torch.

cur.name: Troop helper
cur.reading: A cooperative lineage: Helping Hand strengthens a packmate's attack, Assist borrows a packmate's move, and Fake Out makes an attacker flinch so the group can act first. Fits the ranked packs Monferno lives in, on crags where a troop defends one stretch of cliff together.
cur.behavior: Fights alongside others and covers them; low-ranked animals that make themselves useful.

cur.name: Cliff trickster
cur.reading: A lineage that wins by reading its opponent: Encore locks an attacker into repeating its last move, Counter returns physical blows, and Focus Energy readies a decisive hit. Together they make fights short and predictable. Fits crowded cliff colonies where conflicts are frequent and must not be costly.
cur.behavior: Baits, waits and punishes; rarely the first to commit.

cur.name: Long-dive hunter
cur.reading: Empoleon's diving lineage in the chick: endurance in water, speed and force. The Piplup that stays under longest. Fits deep, cold coastal water.
cur.behavior: Spends more time under the water than on the shore.

cur.name: Tideflat prober
cur.reading: A shore-foraging lineage: mud moves and a quick double jab, a chick that probes mud and shallows instead of diving deep. Fits flat, muddy shores and estuaries.
cur.behavior: Pecks along the tideline; dives only when it must.

cur.name: Shore peacemaker
cur.reading: Empoleon's calming lineage, in the stage that most needs it: moves that soften or confuse a rival without a fight. A Prinplup that can share a shore after all. Fits crowded coasts where loners can't spread out.
cur.behavior: Tolerates neighbours; the first of its age to join a group.

cur.name: Long-dive hunter
cur.reading: The line's diving lineage at its solitary stage: stamina, speed and force underwater. Fits deep, icy seas.
cur.behavior: Rarely seen on land; hunts alone and far out.

cur.name: Long-dive hunter
cur.reading: A lineage built for longer and faster dives: Aqua Ring wraps it in a veil of water that heals it a little each turn, Agility sharpens its speed, and Hydro Pump is a heavy strike at range. Together they extend the ten-minute dives of the canon. Fits deep, cold open water where prey is far down and scattered.
cur.behavior: Dives longer and further offshore than others; rarely seen on land.

cur.name: Shore peacemaker
cur.reading: The adult's restraint made heritable: Feather Dance is a display that sharply lowers an opponent's attack, Yawn makes it drowsy, Supersonic confuses it. Ways to end a dispute without blood. Fits crowded shore colonies where proud animals must live close together.
cur.behavior: Displays and lulls before it ever strikes; more tolerant of neighbours.

cur.name: Tideflat prober
cur.reading: A lineage of mud rather than ice: Mud-Slap and Mud Sport both use mud (one to blind, one to blunt electric attacks), and Double Hit strikes twice in quick succession, like rapid probing. Fits muddy estuaries and tidal flats, a warmer, shallower shore than the canon's icy seas.
cur.behavior: Forages in the shallows at low tide; dives less.

cur.name: Thorn thicket
cur.reading: Roselia's thorn-shooting made heritable and extended: Pin Missile fires a volley of thorns, Spikes scatters barbs on the ground. A lineage that defends a fixed patch, like a dense flowerbed, from browsers and flower thieves rather than hunting. Fits crowded meadow and garden edges where its blooms draw trouble.
cur.behavior: Holds a patch, fires at anything that reaches for a flower, and litters the approach with barbs.

cur.name: Sleeping lure
cur.reading: The scent lure with a sedative behind it: Sleep Powder puts the animal it has drawn in to sleep, Cotton Spore slows anything that tries to leave, and Mind Reader makes the next strike certain. A sit-and-wait trap that needs no venom to work. Fits sheltered pond margins where prey come to drink.
cur.behavior: Lures, drugs and only then strikes; rarely needs to chase.

cur.name: Sun-fed bloom
cur.reading: A lineage that leans on sunlight rather than prey: Synthesis for recovery in the sun, Razor Leaf for everyday defence, Leaf Storm as a single all-out burst that costs it afterwards. Fits open, sunny grassland where prey is scarce and light is not.
cur.behavior: Basks more and lures less; hits hard once when threatened, then retreats to recover.

cur.name: Sand-trap lurker
cur.reading: Three moves that all stop prey getting away: Sand Tomb traps it in sand, Mud Shot and Scary Face slow it. Gible's pounce-from-the-nest canon turned into a whole strategy. Fits sandy or silty cave floors where prey passes the nest mouth.
cur.behavior: Stays at its nest hole longer than most Gible; holds what it catches rather than chasing.

cur.name: Wind-cutter
cur.reading: A lineage that attacks at range from the air: Twister whips up wind and Dragon Breath can paralyse. It is the move version of the Platinum folklore that its wings cut blades of wind. Fits open high country where prey is spotted and hit from a distance.
cur.behavior: Strikes from the air without closing in; leaves flattened brush where it hunts.
cur.note: Built partly on a folklore entry (445.3).

cur.name: Clumsy rampager
cur.reading: Gible's clumsiness made into a temperament: Thrash and Outrage are multi-turn rampages that leave it confused, and Double-Edge hurts the user. A lineage that wins by overwhelming force and pays for it. Fits crowded nesting caves where fights between neighbours are short and violent.
cur.behavior: Fights in frenzies; often injured, rarely beaten.

cur.name: Charming beggar
cur.reading: Snorlax's begging lineage in the young: charm and a lick, a Munchlax that gets food given to it rather than finding it. Fits towns and farms with people who feed it.
cur.behavior: Hangs about kitchens and picnic spots; rarely forages for itself.

cur.name: Larder guard
cur.reading: A lineage that defends its stash: it hits back, braces itself, and chases what runs off with its food. The opposite of the forgetful hoarder in the entries.
cur.behavior: Remembers its stash and keeps it.

cur.name: Canyon runner
cur.reading: Riolu's three-mountains-in-a-night canon made into a lineage: Agility for speed, High Jump Kick for clearing gaps and ledges, Low Kick for taking down heavy animals at the legs. Fits broken canyon country where ground is crossed at a run and in leaps.
cur.behavior: Covers enormous ground every night; strikes from a jump.

cur.name: Reading jaw
cur.reading: A lineage that hunts with its jaws: Mind Reader makes the next move certain to land, and Bite and Crunch put the jaws, otherwise absent from the line's own list, behind it. Aura reading plus a sure bite is the shape of an ambush hunter. Fits forest edge where prey moves under cover.
cur.behavior: Waits until it has read the animal's next movement, then bites once.

cur.name: Pack shield
cur.reading: A guardian lineage: Follow Me draws attacks onto itself, Detect dodges them, and Iron Defense hardens it to take what gets through. It pairs with Riolu's aura alarm: one animal hears the fear and stands in front. Fits open mountainside where a group with young must cross exposed ground.
cur.behavior: Moves toward a frightened groupmate and takes the threat on itself.

cur.name: Nest-raiding pair
cur.reading: The Platinum pair tactic carried in the blood: Fake Out makes a guarding parent flinch, Spite wears down its defences, and Assist lets either partner use the other's moves, so the decoy and the thief can swap roles. Fits snowline forest where tree-nesting birds breed.
cur.behavior: Works in twos; one draws the parents off while the other takes the eggs.

cur.name: Rime sprinter
cur.reading: A first-strike lineage: Ice Shard always goes first, Crush Claw tears and weakens the target's defence, and Double Hit strikes twice. A hunt decided in one rush. Fits open snowfields and ice where prey sees you coming and only speed works.
cur.behavior: Short, explosive chases across open snow; gives up fast if the first rush fails.

cur.name: Cave-mouth tracker
cur.reading: A lineage that hunts what hides or runs: Foresight finds evasive or hidden targets, Pursuit hits harder at prey that tries to flee, and Bite holds what it catches. Fits broken rock and cave entrances like Mt. Silver's, where prey either hides in cracks or bolts.
cur.behavior: Checks every crevice; never lets a fleeing animal go.

cur.name: Sand-trap glider
cur.reading: A lineage that pins prey in sand after the swoop: a trapping sand vortex and a feint to get past a guard. Fits dry, sandy slopes with little cover.
cur.behavior: Lands with its prey and buries it in sand rather than carrying it off.

cur.name: Poison-cross striker
cur.reading: A lineage that leans on its poison: a venomous cross-cut and a critical slash, delivered fast. The line's sting, kept into adulthood. Fits wooded cliffs where prey is quick.
cur.behavior: Strikes on the swoop and leaves; the prey dies later.

cur.name: Glacier relict
cur.reading: The most Mamoswine-like Swinub: Icicle Spear fires icicles in a volley, the tusks-of-ice canon in move form, and Ancient Power is the very move a Piloswine needs to evolve. A lineage that carries its own evolution trigger from the egg. Fits permanent ice, the habitat its ancestors thrived in.
cur.behavior: Grows into a Mamoswine without help; keeps to the coldest ground.

cur.name: Moraine rammer
cur.reading: Piloswine's charging made heavier: Double-Edge and Body Slam are full-weight hits, and Rock Slide brings down stones. A lineage of rocky glacial debris where a charge sends rock tumbling. Fits moraine slopes and scree below ice fields.
cur.behavior: Charges harder and more often; loose rock comes down behind it.

cur.name: Frost-ground breaker
cur.reading: A digger for the hardest ground: Fissure splits the earth, Mud Shot throws wet soil, and Curse makes it slower but stronger and tougher. A lineage that breaks frozen soil to reach buried food, building on Swinub's frozen-ground nose. Fits permafrost tundra where food lies under a hard crust.
cur.behavior: Slow, methodical, leaves cracked and turned ground behind it.
